# J06 — M2.0: the test harness and the per-op test stubs

Plan M2.0, with the two dispatchers split so that no two tasks ever share a file (plan rule: only the owning task
edits its group file; the dispatchers are frozen from here).

Files written (nothing else touched, no Makefile change — J01's wildcards already pick these up):
`ref/real.h`, `test/harness.h`, `test/test_kernels.c`, `test/gradcheck.c`,
`test/k_{misc,norm,act,rope,conv,attn,head,adam}.c` (stubs),
`test/grad_{norm,act,rope,conv,attn,head,gdn,lora}.c` (stubs).

## The interface later tasks use (fixed; do not edit the dispatchers)

* `ref/real.h`: `typedef float real;`, or `double` under `-DJT_REAL_DOUBLE` (the CPU builds ref/ twice, as M2.0 says).
  Also `JT_REAL_IS_DOUBLE`, `JT_RFMT` and the `r_*` math wrappers (`r_sqrt, r_exp, r_expm1, r_log, r_log1p, r_tanh,
  r_pow, r_fabs, r_floor, r_ceil, r_fmin, r_fmax`), each computed in double and rounded back once.
* `test/harness.h` (header-only, all `static inline`): `rnd_fill(x, n, lo, hi, seed)` (xorshift32; the same stream for
  `float*` and `double*`), `rel_err(got, want, n)` / `abs_err(...)` (the M1.2 metric: `max|got-want| /
  max(1e-30, max|want|)`; NaN/inf in `got` is infinitely wrong), `CHECK_REL(name, got, want, n, tol)`,
  `CHECK_ABS(...)`, `CHECK_REL1(name, got, want, tol)`, `CHECK_ABS1(...)`, `dev_upload(host, n) -> float*`,
  `dev_download(dev, host, n)`, `dev_alloc/dev_free/dev_upload_bytes/dev_download_bytes`, `jt_f32_to_bf16` /
  `jt_bf16_to_f32`, `jt_lens_ragged3()` = {1,37,130} / `jt_lens_ragged4()` = {520,670,1026,300} with
  `jt_ragged(lens, nrows, off, row_of) -> tokens`, and the gradcheck core `jt_fd_grad` / `jt_grad_check`.
  Gates: `JT_TOL_FWD 1e-5`, `JT_TOL_BWD 1e-4`, `JT_TOL_GRAD 1e-6`; none is loosened.
* A group returns exactly `JT_OK`, `JT_FAIL` or `JT_NOT_IMPL` (never a failure count) and ends
  `return jt_exit_code();`. That is how a dispatcher tells a stub from a real group. The counter is per translation unit
  (`static` inside a `static inline` accessor), so a group needs no global and no link dependency; `test/test_gdn.c`
  (J16/J17's, its own binary) can include `harness.h` unchanged.
* The gradcheck core: `jt_grad_check(name, f, ctx, x, n, gx, w, nw)` does `L = <w, f(x)>`, the central difference
  `(L(x+he_i) - L(x-he_i))/2h` with `h = 1e-6` over **every** element, and compares against the analytic `gx` with
  `rel < 1e-6`, printing `ok`/`FAIL` and counting. A group only writes one small `static void f(void *ctx, const real *x,
  real *y)` per differentiable input. `jt_grad_check` never takes the null-device shortcut: no device is involved.
* Dispatcher behaviour (all verified, table below): `test_kernels <group>` / `gradcheck <group>` exit 2 on a stub;
  `test_kernels all` fails (1) while any group is a stub, because card-check `m2` runs exactly that; `test_kernels`
  (no arguments, what `make test-null` runs) runs the implemented groups, skips the stubs and exits 0; `gradcheck all`
  (what `make test-cpu` runs) prints `SKIP <group> (not implemented)` and exits 0, but a real failing group still
  fails it. Unknown group / extra argument → usage and exit 2.
* In a shim build without both `TINYNV_HW` and `TINYNV_SOCKET`, `CHECK_REL` and its siblings print
  `ok  <name> (launch only)` and count nothing (verified both ways, below).

Each stub prints `NOT IMPLEMENTED`, returns `JT_NOT_IMPL`, and its comment names the ops and the milestone that owns it.
Replacing a stub means replacing the whole file, keeping the file name, the `int k_<group>(void)` /
`int grad_<group>(void)` name and the return-code contract.

## Notes for the owners of the group files

* `misc` → M2.1, `norm` → M2.2, `act` → M2.3, `rope` and `conv` → M2.4, `attn` and `head` → M2.5, `adam` → M2.6.
  gradcheck has the same groups plus `gdn` (M3.1, J16/J17) and `lora` (M2.6/M5).
* `test_kernels all` is the gate that card-check `m2` runs: it stays red until all eight `k_*.c` are real. That is
  the intended state for now. `make test-null` and `make test-cpu` are green today because they skip the stubs.
* Two output shapes to rely on: `ok  <name> rel=…` for a pass and `FAIL <name> rel=… tol=…` for a failure (plus
  `ok  <name> (launch only)` on the null device); a gradcheck pass/fail line comes from `jt_grad_check` in the same
  shape.
* Sizes for the ragged tests: the M2.0 batches are 168 and 2516 tokens; `jt_ragged` fills `off[nrows+1]` and
  `row_of[tokens]` so the tab / conv / attn groups can share exactly the plan's shapes.
* Nothing here reads real data: only seeds and the two lengths lists from the plan (rule 5).
